short_name: Common comparison unit and design distribution
assumption_text: For the KL dominance bridge, the context-omitting simple, context-omitting complex, and context-aware model classes are evaluated at the same declared comparison unit (trial or participant), against the same omitted-context target law, under the same covariate/design distribution P_V, and P_V is the distribution of the population to which the scientific claim generalizes.
source_or_rationale: Proposed by the L3 KL dominance draft; mixing units or design distributions makes the difference of divergences uninterpretable because the entropy terms no longer cancel (CE-5).
proof_or_analysis_dependency: Required for Theorem L3.2 and for the T-007 threshold corollaries to count units of the declared type.

assumption_text: For the KL dominance bridge, there exist epsilon in (0, 1/2) and a finite T_max such that every per-trial choice probability, under the omitted-context target law and under every candidate model used in the comparison, lies in [epsilon, 1-epsilon] for P_V-almost every covariate value, and no participant contributes more than T_max trials; the unit-level log densities are then uniformly bounded by T_max log(1/epsilon).
source_or_rationale: Proposed by the L3 KL dominance draft; without it the expected divergence can be infinite for some candidates and differences of infima are ill-defined (CE-4). The bound is placed on the per-trial kernel because at the participant unit the response has 2^T support points and a unit-level bound would be unsatisfiable.
proof_or_analysis_dependency: Required for Proposition L3.1, Theorem L3.2, and the differentiation step in Proposition L3.4.
